title: Amortized Bayesian Experimental Design with In-Context Knowledge Conditioning
claim: Standard amortized policies ignore deployment-time knowledge; ours tokenizes external information, filters unreliable parts, and gains when it is reliable.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right: prior diagram, our pipeline, two result curves
description: Three-part figure. The left dashed panel, 'Traditional Amortized BED', shows a loop: Observations and Design boxes connected through a central Policy node (neural-net icon). Prior Info (bell curve, orange) and Auxiliary Data (database icon, purple) feed toward the Policy via dashed gray arrows marked with red X's, meaning they are blocked. The middle panel, 'IMBUE', is a vertical stack. Three input icons (prior, database, observations) become rows of colored tokens (orange, purple, gray), pass through a 'Reliability Filter' where some tokens fade, then a Transformer, and then output a design. A feedback arrow returns the design to the observations. The right panel has two small line plots of EIG. In the first, 'Reliable Information', the blue IMBUE curve is above the dashed gray baseline. In the second, 'Misleading Information', the two curves nearly coincide. A legend sits at the bottom right. Color coding links each knowledge source to its tokens.
caption: Overview of IMBUE. Left: Existing amortized BED policies fail to encode additional information available at deployment. Middle: IMBUE enables in-context adaptation at deployment by encoding external knowledge as additional input tokens, together with a reliability filter that excludes unreliable information. Right: IMBUE accelerates early information acquisition when external information is reliable, and remains robust to misleading information.
abstract: Amortized Bayesian experimental design (BED) enables real-time design strategies by shifting acquisition cost offline, but existing methods remain tied to the prior and task distribution they were trained on and cannot exploit additional information available at deployment. We introduce in-context amortized BED with unified knowledge encoding (IMBUE), a BED framework that admits external knowledge at deployment through a unified in-context interface. IMBUE accepts two forms of such knowledge without retraining, namely user-specified prior knowledge and observations from previous instances of the experiment. Both are encoded as additional input tokens and processed in-context with the accumulated observations by a shared Transformer, and a learned reliability filter scores each external token against the observations and excludes inconsistent ones. Across four benchmarks, IMBUE accelerates early-stage information acquisition when the external knowledge is reliable, and remains close to the no-external baseline when it is not.
